steps: Entered seed CO-UKR-RUTH1 under Play a seed
Played 12 months as Ukraine, mostly picking referendum, treaty and negotiation options
Read the reveal including The truth
Pressed New game and started a second game
scenarios.notes: Mission complete, grade B, 634. The real-world comparison (The truth) answered my wish to see what really happened.

friction.where: Month 2 desk, The move for your mission
friction.expected: A button I cannot afford says so
friction.happened: With 0 political capital left, Choose on Court United States did nothing, no message. Month 3 showed a reason on similar cards (calendar full).
Leaving a crisis open silently picks a named answer (month 2: Emergency security powers, which hurts a goal). Month 1 said it passes with no effect. Inconsistent.

friction.expected: Clear which Choose belongs to which card
friction.happened: Three near-identical Choose buttons; the Defense Minister card text is clipped at the bottom.
It skips the crisis and the mission move; I had to find them in the left list. 'Your call stays open' is unclear wording.
Mission says Washington 36 to 42, the relations line on the same card says United States view of you 34 to 40.
Preview said start next month with 5, then 4 after I added a second order. Consistent but shifting as I click (trust).
Says final score 86 against par 102, the usual for this seat. Two targets, 82 and 102 (trust).
Competent top 10%, Random staff, Do-nothing staff, ladder, Statesman, Beat 634: gamer jargon.
Russia real military strength 1955k vs 1519k, ISW, Kyiv's 20, Better/Worse labels not explained; I did not know what k meant.

friction.where: Month 4 and later phone call cards: Sanae Takaichi, Mark Carney
friction.happened: I knew Merz, Meloni, Macron, Lukashenko; Takaichi and Carney unknown; no explanation on the call cards.
I guessed from the news. Someone who does not follow Ukraine would be lost; 'A guarantee by arsenal' was odd wording.
Dozens of unlabelled round icons (all named Map marker), colours unexplained without opening Guide. Same decision panel as the desk, so I could do everything, but I would never use the map to decide.
Next month button partly cut off at the bottom edge at 1080 high.

friction.expected: See what my last month did
friction.happened: Straight to the reveal; the month 12 result card is never shown.
Negotiate through intermediaries listed as bad because political capital went 3 to 2; a cost is not a failure.
Easy to find; the box opened but I had to tap inside it before typing. Fine.

bugs.title: Choose on an unaffordable order does nothing and says nothing
steps: Open The move for your mission
Press Choose on Court United States
bugs.expected: Disabled with a reason, as the calendar-full cards do

bugs.title: Month 12 result card skipped before the reveal

suggestions.what: Disable or explain Choose when I cannot afford it, everywhere
suggestions.goal_served: R1: never blocked without a plain reason

suggestions.what: Keep The truth, and add a plain-language link to read more on each real event
Replace Competent, Random staff, Do-nothing staff with plain words; explain k
Say who each caller is on the card (Takaichi, Carney)
suggestions.goal_served: R2: an afternoon without a lookup

delight: Month 5 guarantee on paper and month 6 Land for a promise: real dilemmas a history teacher can argue (Budapest memorandum)
Month 6 callback: Remember Hostages in Belarus? Hostages released after secret talks
The truth screen comparing my world with the real one, with sources

fun.reason: Dilemmas were absorbing; months 8 to 10 blurred into pressing Choose all recommended.

clarity.reason: Seven or eight things a month and many Choose buttons; advice cards say who recommends what, which helped, but the left list and right panel repeat each other.

visual.reason: Handsome and readable at 1080p, but much small grey text and clipped cards.

feels_like_a_game.reason: More a briefing exercise than a game; fine for me.

agency.reason: One silent dead button (month 2) and a default answer that applies if I do nothing; otherwise I knew why.

realism.reason: Names, sequence and the Abu Dhabi talks comparison feel real; Ukraine content is accurate.

replay.reason: I would try the Middle East, but not tonight.

recommend.reason: I would tell a friend who reads the news, with a warning about the first month.

verbatim: Finally something that shows me what really happened next to what I did. But I do not know what half the buttons are for until I press them, and Choose should tell me when it will not work.
